text:
james.ng: :rotating_light: EDR alert on dev-ellie01 (ellie.k). Suspicious signed DLL loaded into powershell.exe and immediately quarantined: C:\Windows\Temp\msupdate.dll. Tagging @security-oncall for triage.

security-oncall-bot: New alert created: ALERT-2026-3901 (Severity: high). Detection: Signed DLL with abnormal parent/child. SHA256: d4b7c9a2f3e8c0b1a6f5e9d3c2b1a0f0e9d8c7b6a5f4e3d2c1b0a9f8e7d6c5b4. Process tree: powershell.exe -> rundll32.exe -> msupdate.dll.

ellie.k: I was running a local test of an internal updater script earlier. Laptop was on company VPN. No UAC prompts that I noticed. Quarantine message popped up right after.

mike.s: Oncall here. Can you confirm it's the laptop with disk serial S/N AZ1234 and endpoint id ep-9932? Also, please don't reboot.

ellie.k: yes that's mine, ep-9932. Notified.

james.ng: Pulled EDR artifact and hash above. Quick sigcheck on the file header shows a digital signature, but thumbprint doesn't match any known vendor certs in our allowlist.

security-oncall-bot: Relevant alerts: possible stolen cert (sig present but issuer unusual), suspicious persistence attempt in HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run. Recommended actions: 1) Isolate endpoint from network (EDR isolate). 2) Run full EDR scan and upload artifacts. 3) Snapshot for forensics.

it-support: Initiating isolation now. Ellie, you'll lose VPN shortly. We'll schedule a support call to collect the machine.

ellie.k: ack. I'm finishing a save of my work.

mike.s: While isolated, can you run these commands and paste output to the thread?
```
whoami
Get-AuthenticodeSignature C:\Windows\Temp\msupdate.dll | Format-List *
netstat -ano | findstr 443
```

ellie.k: pasted outputs to the incident ticket (INC-9521). Auth signature output: Status = UnknownError, SignerCertificate: Subject=CN=MSUpdate Co, Thumbprint=5A3C9F... (not matching allowlist). netstat shows an established outbound to 18.205.10.45:443 from pid 3284.

james.ng: 18.205.10.45 resolves to a CDN edge — could be callback. PID 3284 is powershell.exe per EDR process map.

edr-bot: Forensics snapshot completed and uploaded to GCS path: gs://redwood-incidents/INC-9521/snapshots/ep-9932-1769877777.tar.gz.

mike.s: Good. Next: we should check KMS access logs for any key usage from that host/time window. @security-oncall, can you confirm? If attacker had KMS access we'd escalate to infra sec.

security-oncall-bot: Checked KMS audit: no API calls or decrypt operations from ep-9932's IAM principal during the alert window. Affected user does not have KMS admin role.

james.ng: For triage summary: quarantined file appears signed with a dubious cert, powershell spawned remote connection, no KMS compromise. Recommend imaging and reprovisioning dev-ellie01. Also rotate any SSH keys used from that machine as a precaution.

it-support: Imaging scheduled for 2026-05-12 10:00PT. Ellie, please hand in laptop to ops after isolation.

ellie.k: will do. Thanks.

mike.s: Post-incident actions: 1) Add issuer thumbprint to blocked signatures list pending vetting. 2) Add an audit rule to capture SignerCertificate thumbprint on future file loads. 3) Add a quick runbook step to require EDR snapshot before user reboot for suspected signed-but-unknown certs.

james.ng: I'll open GH issue in security-ops repo and PR an allowlist/blocklist change. Also suggest updating onboarding docs to remind devs not to run unsigned installers on workstations.

security-oncall-bot: Incident status: containment complete, remediation planned (imaging), post-incident review scheduled. Incident severity set to S2.

it-support: Closing local ticket once imaging complete and user confirmed.

mike.s: Thanks everyone. Short follow-up: please confirm once Ellie has reprovisioned so we can close INC-9521 and add to monthly incident log. :white_check_mark:
